Rewrote server-startup test discrimination from signal/exit-code to stderr content. Empirical observation: with EOF stdin, both gate-firing and gate-not-firing exit with code 0 (no signal), but only the gate-not-firing path produces [twining] stderr output (dashboard startup, config warnings). The signal-based test was attempting to keep stdin open with a Readable.pipe to force SIGTERM on timeout, but Linux closes the pipe early when the source Readable enters end state. Stderr-content discrimination is platform-independent and 10x faster (343ms vs 3155ms). Rejected: increasing test timeout (doesn't fix root cause), holding stdin open differently with raw fd manipulation (fragile, more code).
